hints.text: Write $2\theta$ as $\theta + \theta$ and use the sum formula.
$\sin(A + B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B$. Put $A = B = \theta$.

explanation: Treat $2\theta$ as $\theta + \theta$ and apply $\sin(A + B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B$.
The two terms are identical, so they combine to $2\sin\theta\cos\theta$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why the tempting answers fail
steps: Choice B gives $2\sin 30^\circ = 1$, and choice D gives the same thing — both wrong.
Choice A gives $2(0.5)(0.866) = 0.866$ ✓. Trig functions do not distribute over multiplication: $\sin(2\theta)$ is never just $2\sin\theta$.
